newsitem.title: USA: U.S. carmakers say Japan fails to open its market.
newsitem.headline: U.S. carmakers say Japan fails to open its market.

text.p: U.S. car dealerships in Japan numbered 103 at the end of last year, below what the U.S. industry said was its "modest" goal of 200, the American Automobile Manufacturers Association said on Friday.
"Japan missed the mark by almost half," AAMA president Andrew Card said in a statement. "Additionally, the plunging yen has added insult to injury."

He said Japan pledged in its 1995 auto agreement with the United States to open its market, and he called on Japanese car-makers to follow through on the pledge and to reassure its car dealers that times had changed.

The association of the Big Three U.S. car makers -- Ford Motor Co, Chrysler Corp and General Motors Corp -- said that American car makers added three new dealer outlets in December, but lost one, leading to a drop in total outlets to 103 since the signing of the auto accord.

Card said, "The yen's excessive depreciation threatens to reignite trade friction between the U.S. and Japan." He urged Japan to move toward a demand-led economic recovery by deregulating its economy, opening its markets and providing greater opportunities for its consumrs.
A first step would be postponement of a scheduled increase in the consumption tax, he said.
